claim: Topbp1 knockout mice reach blastocyst stage but do not progress beyond embryonic day (E) 8, with embryos likely dying at the preimplantation stage.
source: Topbp1 knockout mice exhibit strong defects early in embryonic development, reaching blastocyst stage but not progressing beyond embryonic day (E) 8, with embryos likely dying at the preimplantation stage (Jeon et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jeon et al., 2011, which provides published evidence for this observation.

claim: Conditional knockout of Topbp1 in spermatocytes leads to defects in chromosome synapsis.
source: In the context of meiosis, conditional knockout of Topbp1 in spermatocytes leads to pleiotropic effects, including defects in chromosome synapsis, impaired recruitment of DDR factors to XY chromosomes, defects in condensation of the XY chromosomes, abnormal formation of the sex body, lack of γH2AX spreading to chromatin loops, all of which contribute to a strong MSCI defect as indicated by the complete absence of downstream markers of MSCI, such as USP7, H3K9me3, poly-ubiquitination, and sumoylation (ElInati et al., 2017; Pereira et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to ElInati et al., 2017 and Pereira et al., 2020.

claim: Conditional knockout of Topbp1 in spermatocytes leads to impaired recruitment of DDR factors to XY chromosomes.
source: In the context of meiosis, conditional knockout of Topbp1 in spermatocytes leads to pleiotropic effects, including defects in chromosome synapsis, impaired recruitment of DDR factors to XY chromosomes, defects in condensation of the XY chromosomes, abnormal formation of the sex body, lack of γH2AX spreading to chromatin loops, all of which contribute to a strong MSCI defect as indicated by the complete absence of downstream markers of MSCI, such as USP7, H3K9me3, poly-ubiquitination, and sumoylation (ElInati et al., 2017; Pereira et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to ElInati et al., 2017 and Pereira et al., 2020.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 mice are viable with no difference in body mass compared to wild-type littermates.
source: After validating the point mutations through Sanger sequencing, (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), we found that Topbp1B5/B5 mice were viable, with no difference in body mass when compared to WT littermates (Figure 1B and C)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C comparing body mass between genotypes.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 mice show no sensitivity to ionizing radiation.
source: we found that Topbp1B5/B5 mice were viable, with no difference in body mass when compared to WT littermates (Figure 1B and C), and no sensitivity to ionizing radiation (IR) (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 mice display male-specific infertility.
source: Strikingly, Topbp1B5/B5 mice displayed male-specific infertility (Figure 1E)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E demonstrating breeding outcomes.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 males have a threefold reduction in testis size.
source: Strikingly, Topbp1B5/B5 mice displayed male-specific infertility (Figure 1E), with a threefold reduction in testis size (Figure 1F and G)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and G comparing testis size.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 males have complete lack of spermatozoa.
source: Strikingly, Topbp1B5/B5 mice displayed male-specific infertility (Figure 1E), with a threefold reduction in testis size (Figure 1F and G) and complete lack of spermatozoa (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H showing sperm count.

claim: H&E-stained histological testis sections from Topbp1B5/B5 mice revealed mainly spermatogonia and spermatocytes within the seminiferous epithelium.
source: H&E-stained histological testis sections revealed mainly spermatogonia and spermatocytes within the seminiferous epithelium (Figure 1I)
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 testes have an increased number of TUNEL-positive spermatocytes in seminiferous tubules.
source: H&E-stained histological testis sections revealed mainly spermatogonia and spermatocytes within the seminiferous epithelium (Figure 1I), together with an increased number of TUNEL-positive spermatocytes in seminiferous tubules (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 1J and K.

claim: Cytological evaluation of surface-spread spermatocytes from Topbp1B5/B5 revealed the presence of meiotic prophase I stages from leptonema to pachynema but a total absence of diplonema-staged spermatocytes.
source: Cytological evaluation of surface-spread spermatocytes from Topbp1B5/B5 revealed the presence of meiotic prophase I stages from leptonema to pachynema but a total absence of diplonema-staged spermatocytes (Figure 1L).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytological data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes display normal pachytene entry and no gross defects in chromosome synapsis.
source: Moreover, the staining of the synaptonemal complex proteins SYCP1 and SYCP3 revealed normal pachytene entry and no gross defects in chromosome synapsis, distinct from previous models of ATR and TOPBP1 conditional depletion (ElInati et al., 2017; Widger et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of SYCP1 and SYCP3 staining, with comparison to published models cited.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes reach mid-pachynema, as demonstrated by the accumulation of signal for H1t.
source: Furthermore, unlike reported DDR CKO (conditional knockouts) models such as Rad1 and Brca1 (Abe et al., 2020; Broering et al., 2014; Pereira et al., 2022), Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes reach mid-pachynema, as demonstrated by the accumulation of signal for H1t (Inselman et al., 2003; Figure 1L).
evidence: The claim is supported by H1t staining data shown in Figure 1L and citations to published work.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs showed no sensitivity to hydroxyurea or phleomycin in a long-term cell survival assay.
source: Consistent with the observed organismal viability and the lack of IR sensitivity, Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs showed no sensitivity to hydroxyurea (replication stress) or phleomycin (DSBs) in a long-term cell survival assay (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by clonogenic survival assay data shown in Figure 2A-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs were able to activate DDR signaling responses when challenged with hydroxyurea and phleomycin.
source: Similar to wild-type MEFs, Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs were able to activate DDR signaling responses when challenged with hydroxyurea and phleomycin as demonstrated by the induction of established damage-induced phosphorylation of CHK1, CHK2, RPA2, and KAP1 (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2E demonstrating phosphorylation of DDR markers.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs were able to recruit MDC1 to γH2AX-marked DSB foci when subjected to IR.
source: In addition, Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs were able to recruit MDC1 to γH2AX-marked DSB foci when subjected to IR (Figure 2F)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs showed no increased number of micronuclei compared to Topbp1+/+ MEFs.
source: and showed no increased number of micronuclei, a known marker of defective DDRs (Kwon et al., 2020), when compared to Topbp1+/+ MEFs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by micronuclei quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B, with citation to published work on micronuclei as DDR markers.

claim: Binding of Flag-TOPBP1-B5 to BLM and 53BP1 was impaired.
source: To investigate which, if any, of these interactions are disrupted upon mutating the eight BRCT5 residues, we ectopically expressed Flag-TOPBP1-WT or Flag-TOPBP1-B5 in HEK293T cells. We found that binding of Flag-TOPBP1-B5 to BLM and 53BP1 was impaired, as expected (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: There was a twofold reduction in protein levels of Flag-TOPBP1-B5 compared to Flag-TOPBP1-WT.
source: Moreover, we noticed a twofold reduction in protein levels of Flag-TOPBP1-B5 compared to Flag-TOPBP1-WT, which could be explained by the loss of interaction with BLM (that was proposed to lead to protein stabilization; Balbo Pogliano et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2013) or by protein misfolding caused by the eight K to E/D mutations.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations with potential explanations cited from published work.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes display normal repair of DNA DSBs, with γH2AX staining grossly unchanged at pachynema, being confined only to the XY chromosomes and being excluded from the autosomes.
source: Strikingly, analysis of Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes via meiotic spreads revealed normal repair of DNA DSBs, with γH2AX staining grossly unchanged at pachynema, being confined only to the XY chromosomes and being excluded from the autosomes (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: RAD51 localized only to the X and Y chromosomes during mid-pachytene in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, indicating normal DSB repair at the autosomes.
source: RAD51 localized only to the X and Y chromosomes during mid-pachytene (Figure 3C and D), indicating normal DSB repair at the autosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C and D, with interpretation of the biological significance.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 mutant spermatocytes transit from zygotene into pachytene with normal patterns of HORMAD1 and HORMAD2 localization.
source: We were unable to detect chromosome synapsis abnormalities in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes as Topbp1B5/B5 mutant spermatocytes transit from zygotene into pachytene with normal patterns of HORMAD1 and HORMAD2 localization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: In Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, SYCP1 overlaps with SYCP3 on chromosome cores from all autosomal chromosomes during pachynema.
source: and with SYCP1 overlapping with SYCP3 on chromosome cores from all autosomal chromosomes during pachynema (Figures 1L and 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 1L and 3E.

claim: In Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, the number of MLH1 foci were significantly increased.
source: In Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, while the number of MLH1 foci were significantly increased, the number of MLH3 foci did not differ significantly (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: In Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, the number of MLH3 foci did not differ significantly from wild-type.
source: In Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, while the number of MLH1 foci were significantly increased, the number of MLH3 foci did not differ significantly (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The sex body appeared normal in its shape and was normally formed in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes.
source: The sex body appeared normal in its shape and was normally formed in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 3 and 4A)
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3A and supplementary figures.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes exhibit subtle defects/delays in the spreading of the γH2AX signal on the PAR and pericentromeric regions.
source: exhibiting only subtle defects/delays in the spreading of the γH2AX signal on the PAR and pericentromeric regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4B-G.

claim: The subtle defect in γH2AX spreading accounted for 56% of all γH2AX-stained mid-pachytene cells in Topbp1B5/B5.
source: Although the defect was subtle in its severity, it accounted for 56% of all γH2AX-stained mid-pachytene cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of the defect frequency.

claim: TOPBP1 was normally localized to X and Y chromosomes during prophase I in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes.
source: Importantly, TOPBP1 was normally localized to X and Y chromosomes during prophase I (Figure 3—figure supplement 5, Figure 3F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and Figure 3F-H.

claim: Localization of ATR, BRCA1, MDC1, and 53BP1 in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes spreads was indistinguishable from that observed in Topbp1+/+ spermatocytes.
source: Similarly, localization of the TOPBP1 interactors ATR, BRCA1, MDC1, and 53BP1 in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes spreads was also indistinguishable from that observed in Topbp1+/+ spermatocytes (Figure 4A–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Markers of ATR signaling were mostly normal in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes, as measured by pMDC1 T4, pCHK1 S345, and pHORMAD2.
source: Markers of ATR signaling were also mostly normal, as measured by its canonical targets pMDC1 T4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D), pCHK1 S345 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F), and pHORMAD2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-H.

claim: Phosphorylation of CHK1 on S317 was significantly decreased in Topbp1B5/B5 when compared to Topbp1+/+ spermatocytes.
source: Notably, we did observe that phosphorylation of CHK1 on S317 was significantly decreased in Topbp1B5/B5 when compared to Topbp1+/+ spermatocytes (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 4G and H.

claim: The observed defect in CHK1 S317 phosphorylation is unlikely to be the cause of the infertility observed in Topbp1 B5 mutants.
source: However, since Chek1 CKO spermatocytes complete prophase I and differentiate into spermatozoa, with only minor defects such as a delay in the removal of γH2AX from autosomes (Abe et al., 2018), the observed defect in CHK1 S317 phosphorylation is unlikely to be the cause of the infertility observed in Topbp1 B5 mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from published data on Chek1 CKO phenotypes cited from Abe et al., 2018.

claim: Phosphoproteomic analysis revealed that ATR-dependent signaling is not drastically impaired in Topbp1B5/B5 testes.
source: The resulting plot revealed that ATR-dependent signaling is not drastically impaired in Topbp1B5/B5 testes, as opposed to the marked impairment of ATR signaling previously observed in testes of Rad1 CKO mice (Sims et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data analysis with comparison to published data cited from Sims et al., 2022.

claim: Several phosphorylation sites in the RNA:DNA helicase Senataxin (SETX), including a phosphorylation in the preferred motif for ATR phosphorylation (S/T-Q), were downregulated in Topbp1B5/B5 mice.
source: Nonetheless, our phosphoproteomic analysis did reveal phosphorylation sites mildly disrupted in Topbp1B5/B5 testes compared to Topbp1+/+ testes. In particular, we noticed that several phosphorylation sites in the RNA:DNA helicase, Senataxin (SETX) (Cohen et al., 2018), including a phosphorylation in the preferred motif for ATR phosphorylation (S/T-Q), were downregulated in Topbp1B5/B5 mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 5B, with citation to published work on SETX.

claim: SETX was previously associated with meiotic ATR functions and found to be indispensable for MSCI.
source: Interestingly, SETX was previously associated with meiotic ATR functions and found to be indispensable for MSCI (Becherel et al., 2013; Yeo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Becherel et al., 2013 and Yeo et al., 2015.

claim: Mice treated with the ATR inhibitor AZ20 or lacking Rad1 display reduced phosphorylation of SETX at S/T-Q site and SETX mislocalization during pachynema.
source: Moreover, we recently reported that mice treated with the ATR inhibitor AZ20 or lacking Rad1 display reduced phosphorylation of SETX at S/T-Q site and SETX mislocalization during pachynema (Sims et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sims et al., 2022.

claim: Pachytene spermatocytes from Topbp1B5/B5 display significantly decreased spreading of SETX to XY chromatin loops while still displaying SETX at the unsynapsed axes of the X and Y chromosomes.
source: Consistent with this possibility, we found that pachytene spermatocytes from Topbp1B5/B5 display significantly decreased spreading of SETX to XY chromatin loops while still displayed SETX at the unsynapsed axes of the X and Y chromosomes (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C-F.

claim: Spermatocytes from Topbp1B5/B5 males formed a sex body of grossly normal appearance.
source: Spermatocytes from Topbp1B5/B5 males formed a sex body of grossly normal appearance (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), with undisrupted patterns of the sex body markers CHD4, SUMO, and USP7 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes display normal patterns of chromatin marks including H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27ac, H3K36me3, H3K4me3, H4K16ac, H4ac, H2AK116ub, H3K4me1.
source: Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes also display normal patterns of a range of chromatin marks, including H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27ac, H3K36me3, H3K4me3, H4K16ac, H4ac, H2AK116ub, H3K4me1, as well as proper exclusion of RNA Pol2 from the sex body (Figure 6—figure supplements 2–6).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplements 2-6.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes display proper exclusion of RNA Pol2 from the sex body.
source: Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes also display normal patterns of a range of chromatin marks, including H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27ac, H3K36me3, H3K4me3, H4K16ac, H4ac, H2AK116ub, H3K4me1, as well as proper exclusion of RNA Pol2 from the sex body (Figure 6—figure supplements 2–6).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplements 2-6.

claim: Analysis of Topbp1B5/B5 germ cell population revealed only somatic, spermatogonia, and the initial populations of spermatocytes.
source: In sharp contrast, analysis of Topbp1B5/B5 germ cell population revealed only somatic, spermatogonia, and the initial populations of spermatocytes (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 early-stage spermatocytes could initiate MSCI and promote robust, albeit incomplete, X chromosome silencing.
source: Strikingly, Topbp1B5/B5 early-stage spermatocytes could initiate MSCI and promote robust, albeit incomplete, X chromosome silencing.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis.

claim: Both X and Y chromosomes showed increased gene expression levels in the last spermatocyte stage captured in Topbp1B5/B5 males when compared to RNA from wild-type males.
source: Both X and Y chromosomes showed increased gene expression levels in the last spermatocyte stage captured in Topbp1B5/B5 males when compared to RNA from wild-type males (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 13).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 13.

claim: The expression of X-linked genes at spermatocyte 3 stage was drastically higher in Topbp1B5/B5 males when compared to Topbp1+/+ males.
source: Notably, while we detected only a minor elevation in the levels of X-linked gene expression in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatogonia when compared to Topbp1+/+, the expression of X-linked genes at spermatocyte 3 stage was drastically higher in Topbp1B5/B5 males when compared to Topbp1+/+ males.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis.

claim: Transcriptomics profiles from Topbp1B5/B5 testicular cells showed an increased number of stage 3 spermatocytes (SP3 – pachytene) expressing the spermatocyte-toxic genes Zfy1 and Zfy2 compared to Topbp1+/+.
source: Similar to previous reports based on mutants or treatments that impaired MSCI (Abe et al., 2022; ElInati et al., 2017; Hirota et al., 2018; Modzelewski et al., 2012; Pereira et al., 2022; Royo et al., 2013; Widger et al., 2018), transcriptomics profiles from Topbp1B5/B5 testicular cells showed an increased number of stage 3 spermatocytes (SP3 – pachytene) expressing the spermatocyte-toxic genes Zfy1 and Zfy2 compared to Topbp1+/+ (Figure 6—figure supplements 14 and 15).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplements 14 and 15, with citations to previous reports.

claim: Other genes typically used to illustrate MSCI defects, such as Kdm6a, lamp2, Zfx, Uba1y, and Rhox13, were expressed in a higher number of SP3 cells in Topbp1B5/B5.
source: Other genes typically used to illustrate MSCI defects, such as Kdm6a, lamp2, Zfx, Uba1y, and Rhox13, were also expressed in a higher number of SP3 cells in Topbp1B5/B5 (Figure 6—figure supplements 14 and 15).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplements 14 and 15.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 cells displayed an increased number of SP3 (pachytene) cells expressing Scml2 and displayed an increase in expression levels in these cells compared to Topbp1+/+ testes.
source: In the case of Scml2, Topbp1B5/B5 cells not only displayed an increased number of SP3 (pachytene) cells expressing it but also displayed an increase in expression levels in these cells compared to Topbp1+/+ testes (Figure 6—figure supplements 14 and 15).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplements 14 and 15.

claim: When comparing the spermatocyte 2 to spermatocyte 3 (SP2 to SP3) transition between Topbp1B5/B5 and Topbp1+/+ spermatocytes, 74 genes in Topbp1B5/B5 versus 4 in Topbp1+/+ exhibited reduced silencing.
source: In contrast, when comparing the spermatocyte 2 to spermatocyte 3 (SP2 to SP3) transition between Topbp1B5/B5 and Topbp1+/+ spermatocytes we noticed a major difference in the distribution of the clusters, with 74 genes in Topbp1B5/B5 versus 4 in Topbp1+/+ exhibiting reduced silencing (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: While 134 genes showed unaltered silencing, and only 24 increased silencing in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes during the SP2 to SP3 transition, 43 genes showed unaltered silencing and 185 increased silencing in Topbp1+/+.
source: Moreover, while 134 genes showed unaltered silencing, and only 24 increased silencing in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes during the SP2 to SP3 transition, 43 genes showed unaltered silencing and 185 increased silencing in Topbp1+/+ (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The severity of the silencing defect of a gene had some correlation with its RNA level in the pre-leptotene stage, with highly expressed genes having a higher tendency to have a more severe silencing defect.
source: Notably, the severity of the silencing defect of a gene had some correlation with its RNA level in the pre-leptotene stage, with highly expressed genes having a higher tendency to have a more severe silencing defect (Figure 7G, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 7G and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Topbp1B5/B5 mouse provides a unique model of DDR impairment in which MSCI can be uncoupled from sex body formation.
source: Since the majority of the mouse models of male infertility accumulate pleiotropic defects, with disrupted MSCI and absence of sex body, the Topbp1B5/B5 mouse reported here provides a unique model of DDR impairment in which MSCI can be uncoupled from sex body formation (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented, with reference to Figure 8 summarizing the model.

claim: This is the first DDR mutant that separates XY silencing from sex body formation.
source: This is the first DDR mutant that separates XY silencing from sex body formation, and that separates TOPBP1's role in spermatogenesis from its roles in organismal viability.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and comparison to existing literature.

claim: The B5 allele is the first mutation shown to impair the meiotic silencing function of TOPBP1 in spermatocytes without severely disturbing TOPBP1's role in synapsis and sex body formation.
source: The B5 allele reported here, which carries eight lysine to glutamic/aspartic acid substitutions in BRCT domain 5, is the first mutation shown to impair the meiotic silencing function of TOPBP1 in spermatocytes without severely disturbing TOPBP1's role in synapsis and sex body formation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Topbp1 null mice are embryonic lethal.
source: Consistent with this being a separation of function mutant, Topbp1B5/B5 males are viable and grossly normal, while completely sterile, whereas Topbp1 null, or AAD mutated, mice are embryonic lethal (Jeon et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jeon et al., 2011 and Zhou et al., 2013.

claim: Depletion of TOPBP1 in mammalian cell lines triggers a robust G2/M arrest followed by cell senescence and loss of viability.
source: Moreover, depletion of TOPBP1 in mammalian cell lines triggers a robust G2/M arrest followed by cell senescence and loss of viability (Jeon et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Jeon et al., 2011.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs do not display issues with cell proliferation or DDR defects.
source: Topbp1B5/B5 MEFs do not display issues with cell proliferation or DDR defects.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations on MEFs.

claim: Other mutants previously reported to have XY silencing defects during meiotic prophase I, such as Ago4 null and Dicer CKO, do not result in complete loss of sperm production, but a sub-fertility phenotype.
source: It is important to note that other mutants previously reported to have XY silencing defects during meiotic prophase I, such as Ago4 null and Dicer CKO, do not result in complete loss of sperm production, but a sub-fertility phenotype (Greenlee et al., 2012; Modzelewski et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Greenlee et al., 2012 and Modzelewski et al., 2012.

claim: The set of mutations in B5 disrupt the ability of TOPBP1 to interact with 53BP1 and BLM.
source: Experiments using ectopic expression of Flag-tagged TOPBP1 in HEK293T cells revealed that the set of mutations in B5 disrupt the ability of TOPBP1 to interact with 53BP1 and BLM, as expected from previous reports (Bigot et al., 2019; Blackford et al., 2015; Cescutti et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with citations to previous reports.

claim: The TOPBP1-BLM interaction contributes to protein stabilization.
source: Moreover, we noticed a twofold reduction in protein levels of Flag-TOPBP1-B5 compared to Flag-TOPBP1-WT, which could be explained by the loss of interaction with BLM (that was proposed to lead to protein stabilization; Balbo Pogliano et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Balbo Pogliano et al., 2022 and Wang et al., 2013.

claim: Topbp1 CKO, Rad1 CKO, and Atr CKO spermatocytes display strong synapsis defect and defective entry in pachynema.
source: For example, Topbp1 CKO, Rad1 CKO, and Atr CKO spermatocytes display strong synapsis defect and defective entry in pachynema (ElInati et al., 2017; Widger et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to ElInati et al., 2017 and Widger et al., 2018.

claim: Setx null spermatocytes complete autosomal synapsis, while still displaying MSCI defects.
source: whereas Setx null spermatocytes complete autosomal synapsis, while still displaying MSCI defects.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of published phenotypes of Setx null mice.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes do not share all defects observed in Setx null spermatocytes, as noted by the localization of γH2AX, sumoylation events, ubH2A and ATR at chromatin loops, which are defective in Setx null spermatocytes but normal in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes.
source: On the other hand, is it likely that ATR signaling is controlling a specific aspect of SETX function since Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes do not share all defects observed in Setx null spermatocytes, as noted by the localization of γH2AX, sumoylation events, ubH2A and ATR at chromatin loops, which are defective in Setx null spermatocytes but normal in Topbp1B5/B5 spermatocytes.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of experimental observations with published phenotypes.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes are able to reach the stage of crossover designation with MLH1 positive cells.
source: Moreover, Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes, but not Setx null spermatocytes, are able to reach the stage of crossover designation with MLH1 positive cells.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes progress further in pachynema when compared to Setx null spermatocytes.
source: Taken together, these observations suggest that Topbp1B5/B5 pachytene spermatocytes progress further in pachynema when compared to Setx null spermatocytes
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from experimental observations.

claim: R-loops affect chromatin architecture at promoters and interfere with the recruitment of transcription factors and chromatin remodelers.
source: Moreover, the model predicts that SETX function is specifically affected in the sex body, which is consistent with the observed defect in SETX localization. In support of this model, R-loops affect chromatin architecture at promoters and interfere with the recruitment of transcription factors and chromatin remodelers, as observed in regions harboring CpG islands where R-loops prevent the action of DNA methyltransferases, thus preventing silencing (Santos-Pereira and Aguilera, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Santos-Pereira and Aguilera, 2015.

claim: Highly transcribed genes tend to accumulate more R-loops.
source: Notably, highly transcribed genes, which tend to accumulate more R-loops (Marnef and Legube, 2020), displayed increased silencing defects in the Topbp1B5/B5 mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Marnef and Legube, 2020.
